result.final_text:
## What this letter says
You were in hospital. You had a stomach and bowel infection (acute gastroenteritis). It is resolved.

You also had bleeding in your gut (gastrointestinal bleed). You have long-term swelling in a part of your belly called the mesentery (chronic inflammation). The cause is not known.

Your sickness and loose stools (nausea, vomiting and diarrhea) got better in hospital. You had no belly pain on the day you went home.

Your stool still tested positive for blood (guaiac positive) when you left.

Test results:
- Your hemoglobin was 13.1 when you arrived. It was 10.9 at discharge.
- Your hematocrit was 38.6 when you arrived. It was 31.3 at discharge.
- Your white blood cell count was not high.
- One troponin blood test was negative. Your heart tracing (ECG) showed a normal rhythm.
- Your stool test was negative for Clostridium difficile. It showed a few white blood cells. It also showed a moderate amount of hidden (occult) blood and red blood cells.
- Amylase, lipase, LDH, CRP and liver tests (LFTs) were normal.
- A small calcified spot in the lower left lung (granuloma) apparently is stable. This is not certain.

## What you need to do
1. Take prednisone for 4 weeks, using the plan below. Your gut doctors (GI) asked for this.
2. You can start taking your home medicines again.

## Dates and medicines
The letter gives no dates.

- Prednisone, in hospital: 60 mg by mouth. It was started in hospital.
- Prednisone, week 1: 15 mg by mouth for 7 days.
- Prednisone, week 2: 40 mg for 1 week.
- Prednisone, week 3: 30 mg for 1 week.
- Prednisone, week 4: 20 mg for 1 week. Then the prednisone stops.
- The letter does not say how often to take prednisone.
- The doses are not in a clear order. Week 1 may be a mistake. Please ask your doctor to check.

You can start these home medicines again. The letter gives no dose or timing:
- Prandin
- Actos
- Lipitor
- Glucophage
- Benicar
- Advair

## Questions to ask your doctor
- Are my prednisone doses right? Week 1 says 15 mg.
- How often do I take prednisone each day?
- What dose and timing do I use for my home medicines?
- Will I have a follow-up visit?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
